claim: Electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) single-particle analysis has become an important tool for structural biology of large and flexible macromolecular assemblies.
source: Although electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) single-particle analysis has become an important tool for structural biology of large and flexible macro-molecular assemblies, the technique has not yet reached its full potential.
evidence: This is a general statement about the current state of the field, drawing from established scientific consensus.

claim: Cryo-EM single-particle analysis has not yet reached its full potential.
source: Although electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) single-particle analysis has become an important tool for structural biology of large and flexible macro-molecular assemblies, the technique has not yet reached its full potential.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the limitations discussed in the manuscript.

claim: Radiation damage imposes fundamental limits on cryo-EM resolution.
source: Besides fundamental limits imposed by radiation damage, poor detectors and beam-induced sample movement have been shown to degrade attainable resolutions.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge about radiation damage in cryo-EM.

claim: Poor detectors degrade attainable resolutions in cryo-EM.
source: Besides fundamental limits imposed by radiation damage, poor detectors and beam-induced sample movement have been shown to degrade attainable resolutions.
evidence: This is supported by references to prior work showing detector limitations.

claim: Beam-induced sample movement degrades attainable resolutions in cryo-EM.
source: Besides fundamental limits imposed by radiation damage, poor detectors and beam-induced sample movement have been shown to degrade attainable resolutions.
evidence: This is supported by references to prior work on beam-induced movement.

claim: A new generation of direct electron detectors may ameliorate the effects of poor detectors and beam-induced sample movement.
source: A new generation of direct electron detectors may ameliorate both effects.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential of new technology.

claim: Direct electron detectors exhibit improved signal-to-noise performance compared to conventional detectors.
source: Apart from exhibiting improved signal-to-noise performance, these cameras are also fast enough to follow particle movements during electron irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by prior characterization studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Direct electron detectors are fast enough to follow particle movements during electron irradiation.
source: Apart from exhibiting improved signal-to-noise performance, these cameras are also fast enough to follow particle movements during electron irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by technical specifications and prior studies.

claim: A statistical movie processing approach was developed to compensate for beam-induced movement.
source: Using a newly developed statistical movie processing approach to compensate for beam-induced movement, we show that ribosome reconstructions with unprecedented resolutions may be calculated from almost two orders of magnitude fewer particles than used previously.
evidence: This is supported by the methods described in the manuscript.

claim: Ribosome reconstructions with unprecedented resolutions may be calculated from almost two orders of magnitude fewer particles than used previously using the statistical movie processing approach.
source: Using a newly developed statistical movie processing approach to compensate for beam-induced movement, we show that ribosome reconstructions with unprecedented resolutions may be calculated from almost two orders of magnitude fewer particles than used previously.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The methodology may expand the scope of high-resolution cryo-EM to a broad range of biological specimens.
source: Therefore, this methodology may expand the scope of high-resolution cryo-EM to a broad range of biological specimens.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the future impact of the methodology.

claim: Macromolecular structure determination should in principle be possible to near-atomic resolution from only several thousand projection images of isolated particles in ice.
source: For many years, electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) has held the promise that macromolecular structure determination should in principle be possible to near-atomic resolution from only several thousand projection images of isolated particles in ice (Henderson, 1995; Glaeser, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Henderson (1995) and Glaeser (1999).

claim: Cryo-EM single-particle reconstructions in which protein main-chains may be traced reliably or individual side-chains are well resolved have been limited to large icosahedral viruses.
source: However, cryo-EM single-particle reconstructions in which protein main-chains may be traced reliably or individual side-chains are well resolved have been limited to large icosahedral viruses, and have typically required averaging over millions of asymmetric units (Grigorieff and Harrison, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Grigorieff and Harrison (2011).

claim: Near-atomic resolution cryo-EM reconstructions have typically required averaging over millions of asymmetric units.
source: However, cryo-EM single-particle reconstructions in which protein main-chains may be traced reliably or individual side-chains are well resolved have been limited to large icosahedral viruses, and have typically required averaging over millions of asymmetric units (Grigorieff and Harrison, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Grigorieff and Harrison (2011).

claim: The contrast in EM images is not as good as expected from theory.
source: These results are in accordance with early observations that the contrast in EM images is not as good as expected from theory (Henderson, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Henderson (1995).

claim: The main limiting factor of the information content in cryo-EM data is radiation damage.
source: The main limiting factor of the information content in cryo-EM data is radiation damage: the electron dose needs to be limited to prevent the molecules from disintegrating while they are being imaged.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about radiation damage in cryo-EM.

claim: The electron dose needs to be limited to prevent the molecules from disintegrating while they are being imaged.
source: The main limiting factor of the information content in cryo-EM data is radiation damage: the electron dose needs to be limited to prevent the molecules from disintegrating while they are being imaged.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about radiation damage.

claim: Radiation damage alone is not enough to account for the loss in expected contrast.
source: However, radiation damage alone is not enough to account for the loss in expected contrast.
evidence: This is inferred from the discussion of additional factors affecting contrast.

claim: Poor detective quantum efficiency (DQE) of conventional recording devices contributes to information loss in cryo-EM images.
source: Two additional factors that have been attributed to information loss in cryo-EM images are poor detective quantum efficiency (DQE, a frequency-dependent measure for the signal-to-noise performance) of conventional recording devices, and beam-induced movement or charging of the specimen during imaging (Henderson, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Henderson (1992).

claim: Beam-induced movement or charging of the specimen during imaging contributes to information loss in cryo-EM images.
source: Two additional factors that have been attributed to information loss in cryo-EM images are poor detective quantum efficiency (DQE, a frequency-dependent measure for the signal-to-noise performance) of conventional recording devices, and beam-induced movement or charging of the specimen during imaging (Henderson, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Henderson (1992).

claim: Photographic film has a large field of view and a reasonably good DQE.
source: Traditionally, EM images have been recorded on photographic film, which has a large field of view and a reasonably good DQE, but is not convenient for high-throughput methods due to laborious steps of film development and digitization.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about photographic film properties.

claim: Photographic film is not convenient for high-throughput methods due to laborious steps of film development and digitization.
source: Traditionally, EM images have been recorded on photographic film, which has a large field of view and a reasonably good DQE, but is not convenient for high-throughput methods due to laborious steps of film development and digitization.
evidence: This is based on practical knowledge about film processing.

claim: Over the past decade many electron microscopes have been equipped with charge-coupled device (CCD) cameras.
source: Therefore, over the past decade many electron microscopes have been equipped with charge-coupled device (CCD) cameras.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of technological trends in the field.

claim: CCD cameras allow instant inspection of images.
source: These digital detectors allow instant inspection of the images and are much more convenient in automated data collection schemes, so that large quantities of data may be obtained with relatively little effort (Stagg et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on technical knowledge about CCD cameras.

claim: CCD cameras are much more convenient in automated data collection schemes.
source: These digital detectors allow instant inspection of the images and are much more convenient in automated data collection schemes, so that large quantities of data may be obtained with relatively little effort (Stagg et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stagg et al. (2006).

claim: Large quantities of data may be obtained with relatively little effort using CCD cameras.
source: These digital detectors allow instant inspection of the images and are much more convenient in automated data collection schemes, so that large quantities of data may be obtained with relatively little effort (Stagg et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stagg et al. (2006).

claim: The conversion of electrons into visible light in CCDs comes at the expense of a poorer DQE, in particular at higher voltages.
source: However, the conversion of electrons into visible light that is detected by the CCD comes at the expense of a poorer DQE, in particular at higher voltages where many microscopes operate best.
evidence: This is based on technical knowledge about CCD detector physics.

claim: Most of the near-atomic resolution cryo-EM structures published to date have been recorded on photographic film.
source: Consequently, despite the advantages of CCDs in terms of ease-of-use and data quantity, most of the near-atomic resolution cryo-EM structures published to date have been recorded on photographic film (Grigorieff and Harrison, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Grigorieff and Harrison (2011).

claim: For every elastic scattering event, also three to four inelastic scattering events occur.
source: For every elastic scattering event, which contributes positively to the phase contrast image, also three to four inelastic scattering events occur (Henderson, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Henderson (1995).

claim: Inelastic scattering events deposit energy in the sample, which leads to radiation damage by breaking covalent bonds and the generation of free radicals.
source: The inelastic events deposit energy in the sample, which leads to radiation damage by breaking covalent bonds and the generation of free radicals.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about radiation damage mechanisms.

claim: Inelastic scattering events generate charges in the sample that could lead to image blurring by deflecting the incoming electrons.
source: Besides destroying the very structures one aims to determine, these interactions also generate charges in the sample that could lead to image blurring by deflecting the incoming electrons.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the mechanism of image blurring.

claim: Radiolysis products such as hydrogen gas may build up internal pressure, thus leading to mechanical stress in the sample.
source: In addition, radiolysis products such as hydrogen gas may build up internal pressure, thus leading to mechanical stress in the sample (Leapman and Sun, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Leapman and Sun (1995).

claim: At high electron doses, mechanical stress ultimately leads to bubbling of the sample.
source: At high electron doses this stress ultimately leads to bubbling of the sample, while at much lower doses it has been postulated to induce movements that cause blurring of the images (Glaeser, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Glaeser (2008).

claim: At much lower doses, mechanical stress has been postulated to induce movements that cause blurring of the images.
source: At high electron doses this stress ultimately leads to bubbling of the sample, while at much lower doses it has been postulated to induce movements that cause blurring of the images (Glaeser, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Glaeser (2008) and is explicitly described as a postulation.

claim: Three different companies now sell digital cameras that detect electrons directly.
source: Building on technological developments that were initiated almost a decade ago (Prydderch et al., 2003), three different companies now sell digital cameras that detect electrons directly, that is, without the need to first convert electrons into visible light.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the commercial market for detectors.

claim: Direct electron detectors do not need to first convert electrons into visible light.
source: Building on technological developments that were initiated almost a decade ago (Prydderch et al., 2003), three different companies now sell digital cameras that detect electrons directly, that is, without the need to first convert electrons into visible light.
evidence: This is based on technical knowledge about direct electron detectors.

claim: The DQE of direct electron detectors at high resolution is superior to that of CCD and film.
source: Initial characterization of these direct electron detectors indicated that their DQE at high resolution is superior to that of CCD and film (McMullan et al., 2009a), in particular when backscattering of electrons is reduced by back-thinning of the substrate (McMullan et al., 2009c).
evidence: This is supported by citations to McMullan et al. (2009a) and (2009c).

claim: Backscattering of electrons is reduced by back-thinning of the substrate in direct electron detectors.
source: Initial characterization of these direct electron detectors indicated that their DQE at high resolution is superior to that of CCD and film (McMullan et al., 2009a), in particular when backscattering of electrons is reduced by back-thinning of the substrate (McMullan et al., 2009c).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to McMullan et al. (2009c).

claim: Direct electron detectors record images at high rates: ranging from 16 to 400 images per second for the currently available products.
source: An additional advantage of these devices is that they record images at high rates: ranging from 16 to 400 images per second for the currently available products.
evidence: This is based on technical specifications of available detectors.

claim: Direct electron detectors allow the recording of a video during typical exposures, compared to a single image on film or CCD.
source: This allows the recording of a video during typical exposures, compared to a single image on film or CCD.
evidence: This is based on technical knowledge about detector capabilities.

claim: Grigorieff and colleagues previously showed that beam-induced movements could be followed for large icosahedral viruses by processing videos.
source: By processing these videos, Grigorieff and colleagues previously showed that beam-induced movements could be followed for large icosahedral viruses, although the gain in resolution compared to similar data recorded on film was not as large as expected, possibly due to experimental design (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brilot et al. (2012) and Campbell et al. (2012).

claim: The gain in resolution from video processing compared to similar data recorded on film was not as large as expected, possibly due to experimental design.
source: By processing these videos, Grigorieff and colleagues previously showed that beam-induced movements could be followed for large icosahedral viruses, although the gain in resolution compared to similar data recorded on film was not as large as expected, possibly due to experimental design (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brilot et al. (2012) and Campbell et al. (2012), with speculation about the cause.

claim: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years.
source: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years (Frank et al., 1991), and encompass characteristics that are favorable to cryo-EM structure determination: their large content of dense RNA and their large molecular weight (2.8 MDa for prokaryotic 70S and ∼4 MDa for eukaryotic 80S ribosomes) result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes, and RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Frank et al. (1991).

claim: Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes have a molecular weight of 2.8 MDa.
source: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years (Frank et al., 1991), and encompass characteristics that are favorable to cryo-EM structure determination: their large content of dense RNA and their large molecular weight (2.8 MDa for prokaryotic 70S and ∼4 MDa for eukaryotic 80S ribosomes) result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes, and RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ribosome molecular weights.

claim: Eukaryotic 80S ribosomes have a molecular weight of approximately 4 MDa.
source: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years (Frank et al., 1991), and encompass characteristics that are favorable to cryo-EM structure determination: their large content of dense RNA and their large molecular weight (2.8 MDa for prokaryotic 70S and ∼4 MDa for eukaryotic 80S ribosomes) result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes, and RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ribosome molecular weights.

claim: The large content of dense RNA and large molecular weight of ribosomes result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes.
source: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years (Frank et al., 1991), and encompass characteristics that are favorable to cryo-EM structure determination: their large content of dense RNA and their large molecular weight (2.8 MDa for prokaryotic 70S and ∼4 MDa for eukaryotic 80S ribosomes) result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes, and RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about imaging properties of ribosomes.

claim: RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
source: Ribosome samples have been characterized by cryo-EM for more than 20 years (Frank et al., 1991), and encompass characteristics that are favorable to cryo-EM structure determination: their large content of dense RNA and their large molecular weight (2.8 MDa for prokaryotic 70S and ∼4 MDa for eukaryotic 80S ribosomes) result in images of relatively high contrast compared to many other macromolecular complexes, and RNA is known to be less radiation sensitive than protein.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about radiation sensitivity of biomolecules.

claim: The ribosome is an intrinsically flexible macromolecular machine.
source: On the other hand, the ribosome is an intrinsically flexible macromolecular machine, which often leads to the presence of more than one structural state in ribosome samples.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ribosome structure and dynamics.

claim: Ribosome flexibility often leads to the presence of more than one structural state in ribosome samples.
source: On the other hand, the ribosome is an intrinsically flexible macromolecular machine, which often leads to the presence of more than one structural state in ribosome samples.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ribosome heterogeneity.

claim: Advanced classification techniques are required to separate different ribosome conformations into structurally homogeneous subsets that are amenable to single-particle reconstruction.
source: This represents a challenge, as advanced classification techniques are required to separate the different conformations into structurally homogeneous subsets that are amenable to single-particle reconstruction (Scheres et al., 2007; Fischer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Scheres et al. (2007) and Fischer et al. (2010).

claim: The absence of symmetry in the ribosome makes it necessary to image many more particles than is the case for icosahedral viruses with 60-fold symmetry.
source: In addition, the absence of symmetry in the ribosome makes it necessary to image many more particles (and to determine many more orientations) than is the case for icosahedral viruses with 60-fold symmetry.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the effects of symmetry on particle requirements.

claim: The combination of structural variability and the lack of symmetry may account for the fact that near-atomic resolution cryo-EM maps of ribosome structures have remained elusive thus far.
source: The combination of structural variability and the lack of symmetry may account for the fact that near-atomic resolution cryo-EM maps of ribosome structures have remained elusive thus far.
evidence: This is an inference based on the challenges described.

claim: A 70S T. thermophilus ribosome sample was used to develop image-processing procedures that account for beam-induced movement of individual particles.
source: In the experiments described below, we used a 70S T. thermophilus ribosome sample to develop image-processing procedures that account for beam-induced movement of individual particles.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental methods described in the manuscript.

claim: The detector operates at a rate of 17 frames per second.
source: Our detector operates at a rate of 17 frames per second, and we recorded 16-frame videos during 1-s exposures.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the detector used.

claim: 16-frame videos were recorded during 1-s exposures.
source: Our detector operates at a rate of 17 frames per second, and we recorded 16-frame videos during 1-s exposures.
evidence: This is an experimental parameter described in the methods.

claim: At a total dose of 16 electrons/Å2, each individual video frame integrates less than 1 electron/Å2.
source: At a total dose of 16 electrons/Å2, each individual video frame therefore integrates less than 1 electron/Å2.
evidence: This is calculated from the experimental parameters.

claim: High noise levels in individual video frames were expected to pose severe limitations on the accuracy with which these frames may be aligned.
source: We expected the high noise levels in these individual frames to pose severe limitations on the accuracy with which these frames may be aligned.
evidence: This is a speculation based on signal-to-noise considerations.

claim: An entire data set was collected as tilted pairs to experimentally assess alignment errors for video frames.
source: Because the alignment accuracy of individual particles remains unknown in typical single-particle analysis, we collected an entire data set as tilted pairs and used tilt-pair analysis to experimentally assess alignment errors for video frames (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This is an experimental design choice described in the methods.

claim: Tilt-pair analysis was used to experimentally assess alignment errors for video frames.
source: Because the alignment accuracy of individual particles remains unknown in typical single-particle analysis, we collected an entire data set as tilted pairs and used tilt-pair analysis to experimentally assess alignment errors for video frames (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rosenthal and Henderson (2003) and the experimental data.

claim: A statistical video processing procedure was developed that does not depend on tilted images.
source: Guided by the results obtained from this analysis, we then developed a statistical video processing procedure that does not depend on tilted images.
evidence: This is supported by the methods described in the manuscript.

claim: Tilt pairs of videos were recorded on the 70S T. thermophilus ribosome sample.
source: We recorded tilt pairs of videos on the 70S T. thermophilus ribosome sample and used 2D and 3D classification to select a structurally homogeneous subpopulation of 15,202 particle pairs for 3D reconstruction (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the results.

claim: 2D and 3D classification were used to select a structurally homogeneous subpopulation of 15,202 particle pairs for 3D reconstruction.
source: We recorded tilt pairs of videos on the 70S T. thermophilus ribosome sample and used 2D and 3D classification to select a structurally homogeneous subpopulation of 15,202 particle pairs for 3D reconstruction (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is an experimental procedure and result described in the manuscript.

claim: An alignment precision for the tilt pairs of 2° was estimated by assessing the consistency between the orientations from independently refined tilt pair particles with the known microscope tilt geometry.
source: By assessing the consistency between the orientations from independently refined tilt pair particles with the known microscope tilt geometry, we estimated an alignment precision for the tilt pairs of 2° (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2A and the method cited from Rosenthal and Henderson (2003).

claim: The 2° alignment precision is a significant improvement over the 4° precision reported for a similar sample recorded on CCD.
source: This is a significant improvement over the 4° precision reported for a similar sample recorded on CCD (Henderson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Henderson et al. (2011) and comparison with the current results.

claim: The improvement in alignment precision reflects the improved signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) in the individual particles, which are a direct consequence of the improved DQE of the detector.
source: This improvement reflects the improved signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) in the individual particles, which are a direct consequence of the improved DQE of the detector.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between DQE and SNR.

claim: Averaging images with higher SNRs requires fewer particles to overcome the noise.
source: The benefits of using particles with higher SNRs for structure determination are therefore twofold. On the one hand, averaging images with higher SNRs requires fewer particles to overcome the noise.
evidence: This is based on established principles of signal averaging.

claim: Higher SNRs result in smaller alignment errors, which then lead to decreased blurring in the reconstruction.
source: On the other hand, higher SNRs result in smaller alignment errors, which then lead to decreased blurring in the reconstruction.
evidence: This is based on established principles of image alignment and reconstruction.

claim: Both effects of higher SNRs will lead to higher-resolution maps from fewer particles.
source: Both effects will lead to higher-resolution maps from fewer particles, which explains the relatively high resolution of 6.5 Å that we obtained from only 15,202 particle pairs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined effects described.

claim: A resolution of 6.5 Å was obtained from only 15,202 particle pairs using 16-frame averages.
source: Both effects will lead to higher-resolution maps from fewer particles, which explains the relatively high resolution of 6.5 Å that we obtained from only 15,202 particle pairs.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: Each original 16-frame average particle was partitioned into multiple independent particles that were calculated as the average of a varying number of individual video frames.
source: We then assessed how accurately particle movement may be followed during the electron exposure. To this purpose, we partitioned each original 16-frame average particle into multiple independent particles that were calculated as the average of a varying number of individual video frames.
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the results.

claim: Four additional data sets were artificially created, comprising averages of 2 × 8, 3 × 6, 4 × 4 or 8 × 2 video frames for each original particle.
source: In this manner, we artificially created four additional data sets of increasing size, comprising averages of 2 × 8, 3 × 6, 4 × 4 or 8 × 2 video frames for each original particle.
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the results.

claim: The numbers of correctly aligned particles as well as the alignment precision decrease with averaging over fewer video frames.
source: Tilt-pair analysis for these data showed that, as expected, the numbers of correctly aligned particles as well as the alignment precision decrease with averaging over fewer video frames (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Particles that were calculated from later video frames tend to align less accurately, most likely as a result of accumulated radiation damage.
source: In addition, we noted a trend for particles that were calculated from later video frames to align less accurately, most likely as a result of accumulated radiation damage.
evidence: This is an observation from the data with a speculative explanation.

claim: The best reconstructions, at 5.4 Å resolution, were obtained when using averages of six or four individual video frames.
source: To assess the effects of these alignment errors on reconstruction quality, we also inspected the Fourier Shell Correlation (FSC) curves that were reported for the four refinements (Figure 2C). The best reconstructions, at 5.4 Å resolution, were obtained when using averages of six or four individual video frames, which apparently represent the optimum between accurately describing particle movement and not introducing too large alignment errors for these data.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Averages of six or four individual video frames represent the optimum between accurately describing particle movement and not introducing too large alignment errors for these data.
source: The best reconstructions, at 5.4 Å resolution, were obtained when using averages of six or four individual video frames, which apparently represent the optimum between accurately describing particle movement and not introducing too large alignment errors for these data.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Overall rotations and translations during the exposure are in the order of 1.7 ± 1.2° and 4.2 ± 2.3 Å, respectively.
source: Analysis of the orientations for the four-frame averaged particles that were aligned correctly according to the tilt-pair analysis revealed that overall rotations and translations during the exposure are in the order of 1.7 ± 1.2° and 4.2 ± 2.3 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the analysis of particle movements.

claim: Complicated patterns of movement for particles on some of the illuminated areas indicate that the observed movements were not merely the result of a drifting stage.
source: Complicated patterns of movement for particles on some of the illuminated areas (e.g., see white lines in Figure 1A) indicate that the observed movements were not merely the result of a drifting stage, but more likely to be attributed to, as yet poorly understood, beam-induced effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed movement patterns shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The observed movements were more likely to be attributed to, as yet poorly understood, beam-induced effects.
source: Complicated patterns of movement for particles on some of the illuminated areas (e.g., see white lines in Figure 1A) indicate that the observed movements were not merely the result of a drifting stage, but more likely to be attributed to, as yet poorly understood, beam-induced effects.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed movement patterns.

claim: Beam-induced movements are relatively small.
source: The observations that beam-induced movements are relatively small, and that the 16-frame averages may be aligned most accurately, represent valuable prior knowledge that may be efficiently expressed using statistical refinement methods.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations of particle movements.

claim: 16-frame averages may be aligned most accurately.
source: The observations that beam-induced movements are relatively small, and that the 16-frame averages may be aligned most accurately, represent valuable prior knowledge that may be efficiently expressed using statistical refinement methods.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A probabilistic prior on the orientations of the video frames was implemented inside a Bayesian refinement approach.
source: In the 'Materials and methods' section we describe the implementation of a probabilistic prior on the orientations of the video frames inside a Bayesian refinement approach (Scheres, 2012a).
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the manuscript.

claim: The prior down-weights orientations for the video frames in a continuous manner according to their distance from the orientation determined for the 16-frame averages.
source: This prior down-weights orientations for the video frames in a continuous manner according to their distance from the orientation determined for the 16-frame averages.
evidence: This is a description of the statistical method developed.

claim: Application of the statistical video processing procedure to the 70S ribosome data yielded a reconstruction with a resolution of 5.1 Å.
source: Application of this procedure to the 70S ribosome data yielded a reconstruction with a resolution of 5.1 Å (orange line in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Reconstruction quality may be improved by following the movement of individual particles.
source: Comparison of the FSCs between the reconstructed maps and a rigid-body fitted crystal structure (Selmer et al., 2006), decreasing estimated B-factors, and visual inspection of the maps all confirmed that reconstruction quality may be improved by following the movement of individual particles, and that the statistical approach outperforms the straightforward use of multi-frame averaged particles in this respect (Figure 2D–F, Figure 2–figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including FSC curves, B-factors, and visual inspection shown in the figures.

claim: The statistical approach outperforms the straightforward use of multi-frame averaged particles.
source: Comparison of the FSCs between the reconstructed maps and a rigid-body fitted crystal structure (Selmer et al., 2006), decreasing estimated B-factors, and visual inspection of the maps all confirmed that reconstruction quality may be improved by following the movement of individual particles, and that the statistical approach outperforms the straightforward use of multi-frame averaged particles in this respect (Figure 2D–F, Figure 2–figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: A second, untilted data set was collected on an 80S S.cerevisiae ribosome sample during a single, manual microscopy session.
source: Finally, the developed procedure was applied to a second, untilted data set that was collected on an 80S S.cerevisiae ribosome sample during a single, manual microscopy session.
evidence: This is an experimental procedure described in the results.

claim: Classification of the 80S data identified two major conformations, comprising 35,813 and 22,638 particles, respectively.
source: Classification identified two major conformations, comprising 35,813 and 22,638 particles, respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the classification analysis.

claim: A difference of ∼2° in ratchet-like movement represents the largest difference between the two 80S classes.
source: A difference of ∼2° in ratchet-like movement represents the largest difference between the two classes (also see Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by Video 1.

claim: Using the statistical video processing procedure, refinement of 80S class 1 yielded a map with an overall resolution of 4.5 Å.
source: Using the statistical video processing procedure, refinement of class 1 yielded a map with an overall resolution of 4.5 Å, while class 2 yielded a 4.6 Å map (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Using the statistical video processing procedure, refinement of 80S class 2 yielded a 4.6 Å map.
source: Using the statistical video processing procedure, refinement of class 1 yielded a map with an overall resolution of 4.5 Å, while class 2 yielded a 4.6 Å map (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Both 80S maps exhibited signs of unresolved structural heterogeneity, in particular in the small subunit and most notably for class 1.
source: However, both maps still exhibited signs of unresolved structural heterogeneity, in particular in the small subunit and most notably for class 1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The overall resolution estimates for the 80S maps are too optimistic for the disordered parts.
source: Therefore, the overall resolution estimates are too optimistic for the disordered parts, whereas the most stable parts of the structures still contain significant information beyond the overall estimated resolutions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed heterogeneity.

claim: The most stable parts of the 80S structures still contain significant information beyond the overall estimated resolutions.
source: Therefore, the overall resolution estimates are too optimistic for the disordered parts, whereas the most stable parts of the structures still contain significant information beyond the overall estimated resolutions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed quality of the density in different regions.

claim: The density for the 60S subunit clearly shows separation of β-strands, the pitch of α-helices, density for many side chains, and the separation of RNA bases.
source: The density for the 60S subunit clearly shows separation of β-strands, the pitch of α-helices, density for many side chains, and the separation of RNA bases, indicating that useful information to ∼4 Å resolution is present in the best parts of the map (Figure 3C–G, Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 3C-G and Video 2.

claim: Useful information to ∼4 Å resolution is present in the best parts of the 80S map.
source: The density for the 60S subunit clearly shows separation of β-strands, the pitch of α-helices, density for many side chains, and the separation of RNA bases, indicating that useful information to ∼4 Å resolution is present in the best parts of the map (Figure 3C–G, Video 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed features in the density map.

claim: The level of detail in the density for the 40S subunit varies, but is generally lower than for the 60S subunit.
source: The level of detail in the density for the 40S subunit varies, but is generally lower than for the 60S subunit (Figure 3H,I, Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 3H-I and Video 2.

claim: Calculation of FSC curves between the cryo-EM maps and rigid-body fitted crystal structures for the 60S and 40S subunits confirmed the estimated resolutions.
source: Calculation of FSC curves between the cryo-EM maps and rigid-body fitted crystal structures for the 60S and 40S subunits (Ben-Shem et al., 2011) confirmed the estimated resolutions, as well as the variation in quality of the density across the maps (Figure 3J,K).
evidence: This is supported by the FSC curves shown in Figure 3J-K.

claim: Calculation of FSC curves between the cryo-EM maps and rigid-body fitted crystal structures confirmed the variation in quality of the density across the maps.
source: Calculation of FSC curves between the cryo-EM maps and rigid-body fitted crystal structures for the 60S and 40S subunits (Ben-Shem et al., 2011) confirmed the estimated resolutions, as well as the variation in quality of the density across the maps (Figure 3J,K).
evidence: This is supported by the FSC curves shown in Figure 3J-K.

claim: The reconstructions presented in this paper are of significantly higher resolution than any prokaryotic or eukaryotic ribosome structures that were calculated from cryo-EM data on photographic film or CCD.
source: The reconstructions presented in this paper are of significantly higher resolution than any prokaryotic or eukaryotic ribosome structures that were calculated from cryo-EM data on photographic film or CCD.
evidence: This is a comparative claim based on the results and knowledge of prior work.

claim: The reconstructions were obtained from unprecedented small numbers of particles.
source: Moreover, they were obtained from unprecedented small numbers of particles.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results and comparison with prior work.

claim: Currently the highest resolution ribosome map in the EMDB (an 80S structure from the plant Triticum aestivum) was calculated from almost 1.4 million particles and was reported to be at 5.5 Å resolution.
source: For comparison, currently the highest resolution ribosome map in the EMDB (an 80S structure from the plant Triticum aestivum) was calculated from almost 1.4 million particles and was reported to be at 5.5 Å resolution (Armache et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Armache et al. (2010).

claim: Reconstructions with useful information up to ∼4 Å resolution were obtained from nearly two orders of magnitude fewer particles than the 1.4 million particles used for the previous highest resolution ribosome map.
source: We obtained reconstructions with useful information up to ∼4 Å resolution from nearly two orders of magnitude fewer particles.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results and comparison with prior work.

claim: Maps with useful information up to 90% of the Nyquist frequency were calculated.
source: The observation that we could calculate maps with useful information up to 90% of the Nyquist frequency surpassed our initial expectations and clearly illustrates the potential of direct electron detectors combined with adequate video processing for cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results.

claim: The ability to calculate maps with useful information up to 90% of the Nyquist frequency surpassed initial expectations.
source: The observation that we could calculate maps with useful information up to 90% of the Nyquist frequency surpassed our initial expectations and clearly illustrates the potential of direct electron detectors combined with adequate video processing for cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence: This is a statement about the authors' expectations versus the actual results.

claim: The results clearly illustrate the potential of direct electron detectors combined with adequate video processing for cryo-EM structure determination.
source: The observation that we could calculate maps with useful information up to 90% of the Nyquist frequency surpassed our initial expectations and clearly illustrates the potential of direct electron detectors combined with adequate video processing for cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Incorporation of the new detectors into automated data collection schemes will result in much larger amounts of data than used in this study.
source: Incorporation of the new detectors into automated data collection schemes will result in much larger amounts of data than we have used in our study.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications.

claim: For relatively high molecular-weight complexes that display sufficient contrast for accurate alignment and classification, larger amounts of data may allow high-resolution reconstruction of many more structural states.
source: For relatively high molecular-weight complexes that display sufficient contrast for accurate alignment and classification, this may then allow high-resolution reconstruction of many more structural states, or of states that are adopted by only a small fraction of the particles.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications.

claim: If the sample is sufficiently rigid to exist in only one or a few distinct states, then larger amounts of data are expected to lead to even higher resolutions than the ones reported here.
source: Moreover, if the sample is sufficiently rigid to exist in only one or a few distinct states, then larger amounts of data are expected to lead to even higher resolutions than the ones reported here.
evidence: This is a speculation based on theoretical considerations.

claim: Following SNR considerations, an overall resolution of 4.5 Å would increase to ∼3.3 Å if the approach were applied to 1 million particles of similar quality.
source: For example, following the SNR considerations proposed by (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003), our overall resolution of 4.5 Å would increase to ∼3.3 Å if we would apply our approach to 1 million particles of similar quality (provided no other resolution-degrading factors play a role).
evidence: This is a speculation based on theoretical considerations from Rosenthal and Henderson (2003).

claim: The combination of direct electron detectors, video processing approaches, and automated data collection schemes will significantly increase the number of specimens for which de novo building of atomic models into cryo-EM maps becomes feasible.
source: Therefore, we foresee that the combination of direct electron detectors, video processing approaches, and automated data collection schemes will significantly increase the number of specimens for which de novo building of atomic models into cryo-EM maps becomes feasible.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future impact of the technology.

claim: The advantages of direct electron detectors and video processing procedures are not limited to relatively large complexes alone.
source: The advantages of direct electron detectors and video processing procedures are not limited to relatively large complexes alone.
evidence: This is an inference based on the discussion of applications to smaller complexes.

claim: Current alignment procedures are often severely limited by low SNRs in images of complexes that are smaller than ∼300 to 500 kDa.
source: Current alignment procedures are often severely limited by low SNRs in images of complexes that are smaller than ∼300 to 500 kDa.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about limitations in cryo-EM.

claim: SNRs in individual particles drop quickly with increasing spatial frequency.
source: Because SNRs in individual particles drop quickly with increasing spatial frequency image alignments are typically mainly driven by the lower-resolution components in the images (Henderson et al., 2011; Scheres and Chen, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Henderson et al. (2011) and Scheres and Chen (2012).

claim: Image alignments are typically mainly driven by the lower-resolution components in the images.
source: Because SNRs in individual particles drop quickly with increasing spatial frequency image alignments are typically mainly driven by the lower-resolution components in the images (Henderson et al., 2011; Scheres and Chen, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Henderson et al. (2011) and Scheres and Chen (2012).

claim: Lower-resolution components have been observed to remain intact after much higher electron doses than the high-resolution information.
source: These components have been observed to remain intact after much higher electron doses than the high-resolution information (Hayward and Glaeser, 1979; Baker and Rubinstein, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hayward and Glaeser (1979) and Baker and Rubinstein (2010).

claim: Relatively long videos with a high dose could be used to obtain reliable low-resolution components.
source: Therefore, relatively long videos with a high dose could be used to obtain reliable low-resolution components, while a dose-dependent weighting scheme to account for radiation damage may be used to optimize the SNR for higher spatial frequencies at the same time (Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculation about future methodological approaches, with a citation to Campbell et al. (2012).

claim: A dose-dependent weighting scheme to account for radiation damage may be used to optimize the SNR for higher spatial frequencies.
source: Therefore, relatively long videos with a high dose could be used to obtain reliable low-resolution components, while a dose-dependent weighting scheme to account for radiation damage may be used to optimize the SNR for higher spatial frequencies at the same time (Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculation about future methodological approaches, with a citation to Campbell et al. (2012).

claim: Such procedures are expected to significantly lower the size limit of particles that may still be aligned correctly and are thus amenable to cryo-EM structure determination.
source: Such procedures are expected to significantly lower the size limit of particles that may still be aligned correctly and are thus amenable to cryo-EM structure determination.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future impact of the proposed procedures.

claim: Accurately following the movement of small particles during videos will be more challenging than for the high-contrast ribosome particles presented here.
source: Still, accurately following the movement of small particles during videos will be more challenging than for the high-contrast ribosome particles presented here.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between particle size, contrast, and alignment accuracy.

claim: In order to also obtain near-atomic resolutions for smaller particles, further investigations into the nature of beam-induced image blurring and how to stop it will still be necessary.
source: Therefore, in order to also obtain near-atomic resolutions for smaller particles, further investigations into the nature of beam-induced image blurring and how to stop it will still be necessary.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research needs.

source: Also these investigations are expected to benefit significantly from the possibility to analyze beam-induced movements during videos recorded by direct electron detectors.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research approaches.

claim: Currently available detectors, combined with video processing algorithms like the one presented here, will result in higher-resolution cryo-EM structures for many more samples than those reported until now.
source: Currently available detectors, combined with video processing algorithms like the one presented here, will result in higher-resolution cryo-EM structures for many more samples than those reported until now.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future impact of the technology.

claim: Cryo-EM image quality will keep improving as ongoing technological developments such as single-electron counting detectors, phase-plate imaging and better sample preparation techniques mature.
source: Meanwhile, cryo-EM image quality will keep improving as ongoing technological developments such as single-electron counting detectors (McMullan et al., 2009b), phase-plate imaging (Nagayama, 2011) and better sample preparation techniques mature.
evidence: This is a speculation about future technological developments, with citations to McMullan et al. (2009b) and Nagayama (2011).

claim: The field will continue to progress towards fulfilling the promise of providing near-atomic resolution reconstructions for a wide range of specimens.
source: Therefore, we are optimistic that the field will continue to progress towards fulfilling the promise of providing near-atomic resolution reconstructions, and thereby more detailed biological insights, for a wide range of specimens.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future of the field.

claim: Near-atomic resolution reconstructions will provide more detailed biological insights for a wide range of specimens.
source: Therefore, we are optimistic that the field will continue to progress towards fulfilling the promise of providing near-atomic resolution reconstructions, and thereby more detailed biological insights, for a wide range of specimens.

source: 70S T. thermophilus ribosome samples with tRNAs and mRNA were produced as described previously (Selmer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a methodological detail with a citation to Selmer et al. (2006).

source: 80S ribosomes were purified from S. cereviseae strain YAS-2488.

source: All ribosomal proteins, as well as the protein Stm1, were identified using mass spectrometry.

claim: Grids were blotted for 2.5 s and plunge-frozen in liquid ethane using an FEI Vitrobot.
source: Grids were blotted for 2.5 s and plunge-frozen in liquid ethane using an FEI Vitrobot.

source: Grids were transferred to an FEI Polara G2 microscope that was operated at 300 kV.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

source: Using an extraction voltage of 3900 V, a gun lens setting of 2 and a spotsize of 4 or 5, an estimated dose of 16 electrons/Å2 was applied during 1-s exposures.

claim: Images were recorded at the approximate center of the hole on a back-thinned FEI Falcon detector at a calibrated magnification of 79,096 (yielding a pixel size of 1.77 Å).
source: Images were recorded at the approximate center of the hole on a back-thinned FEI Falcon detector at a calibrated magnification of 79,096 (yielding a pixel size of 1.77 Å).

source: All data were collected manually during two half-day sessions for the 70S sample, and a single half-day session for the 80S sample.

source: A total of 24,044 70S particle pairs and 72,447 80S particles were selected using the swarm tool in the e2boxer.py program of EMAN2 (Tang et al., 2007), contrast transfer function parameters were estimated using CTFFIND3 (Mindell and Grigorieff, 2003), and all 2D and 3D classifications and refinements were performed in RELION (Scheres, 2012b).

claim: A total of 72,447 80S particles were selected using the swarm tool in the e2boxer.py program of EMAN2.
source: A total of 24,044 70S particle pairs and 72,447 80S particles were selected using the swarm tool in the e2boxer.py program of EMAN2 (Tang et al., 2007), contrast transfer function parameters were estimated using CTFFIND3 (Mindell and Grigorieff, 2003), and all 2D and 3D classifications and refinements were performed in RELION (Scheres, 2012b).
evidence: This is a methodological detail with citations.

claim: Contrast transfer function parameters were estimated using CTFFIND3.
source: A total of 24,044 70S particle pairs and 72,447 80S particles were selected using the swarm tool in the e2boxer.py program of EMAN2 (Tang et al., 2007), contrast transfer function parameters were estimated using CTFFIND3 (Mindell and Grigorieff, 2003), and all 2D and 3D classifications and refinements were performed in RELION (Scheres, 2012b).

source: For the 70S data set, discarded particles included 50S subunits and 70S ribosomes with tRNAs in the E- and P-sites, and 15,202 particles were selected to correspond to 70S ribosomes with a single tRNA in the P-site.

claim: 15,202 particles were selected to correspond to 70S ribosomes with a single tRNA in the P-site.

claim: Initial 3D classification of the 80S data did not yield structurally distinct classes.
source: For the 80S data, dissociated subunits could again be identified in the 2D class averages, but initial 3D classification did not yield structurally distinct classes.

source: However, after 3D refinement of a single model, blurry density for the 40S subunit indicated that significant structural heterogeneity was still present.

source: This calculation separated two conformations with different degrees of ratchet-like movement, comprising 35,813 and 22,638 particles, respectively.

source: Prior to visualization, all density maps were corrected for the modulation transfer function (MTF) of the detector, and then sharpened by applying a negative B-factor that was estimated using automated procedures (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).

claim: All density maps were sharpened by applying a negative B-factor that was estimated using automated procedures.

claim: Continuous density for RNA nucleotides 440–499 of expansion segment 7 and nucleotides 1954–2093 of expansion segment 27 in 25S was observed, which were not modelled in the 80S crystal structure.
source: To allow others to mine our structures for additional information (e.g., we see continuous density for RNA nucleotides 440–499 of expansion segment 7 and nucleotides 1954–2093 of expansion segment 27 in 25S, which were not modelled in the 80S crystal structure), we have deposited our maps at the EMDB (accession numbers 2275, 2276 and 2277).

claim: The maps have been deposited at the EMDB (accession numbers 2275, 2276 and 2277).

claim: Gaussian prior distributions were defined on the rotations and translations of the video frames.
source: A novel procedure for video-frame alignment was developed that exploits the relatively high accuracy of aligning 16-frame average particles (Figure 2B), as well as the prior knowledge that particles are unlikely to undergo very large rotations or translations during the 1-s exposure. To this purpose, we defined Gaussian prior distributions on the rotations and translations of the video frames, and centered these distributions at the observed orientations for alignments with the corresponding 16-frame average particles.
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the manuscript.

claim: The Gaussian priors were centered at the observed orientations for alignments with the corresponding 16-frame average particles.
source: To this purpose, we defined Gaussian prior distributions on the rotations and translations of the video frames, and centered these distributions at the observed orientations for alignments with the corresponding 16-frame average particles.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: The priors were incorporated as prior probability distributions in the Bayesian refinement approach of the RELION program.
source: The priors were then incorporated as prior probability distributions, P(φ|Θ,Y) in Eq. 7 of Scheres (2012a), in the Bayesian refinement approach of the RELION program.
evidence: This is a methodological detail with a citation to Scheres (2012a).

claim: A standard deviation of 1° for the priors on the Euler angles was used for all calculations shown in this paper.
